content.text:
I built the reusable Skill and ran it on all six employers. Every source file and the classification guide were reachable from the links Nadia gave in the interview, so nothing had to be left as groundwork. The interview export is committed unchanged, and nothing was pushed. All 13 unit tests pass and the format validator passes 165 of 165 checks.

## What the Skill does
- **Reads the sources fresh on every run** from Nadia's Drive links, using only Python's standard library.
- **Uses only the company guide's own paragraph numbers** (CG-04 and so on) in `rationale_ref`. Nadia said she didn't know of identifiers, but the guide prints them and the assignment requires them.
- **Applies house practice only as Nadia stated it.** I wrote her rules down with interview timestamps in [house-practice.md](skills/class-code-assistant/references/house-practice.md). Six places where I had to interpret her words are labelled as my readings, and each one becomes an open item wherever it changes an allocation.
- **Keeps judgment separate from arithmetic.** The judgments sit in one worksheet per employer, each citing the record it rests on. The engine then applies the thresholds, splits, flat amounts, caps and subcontractor share the same way for every employer. No employer data is in the code, and the validator checks that.
- **Produces the required outputs:** the six [codes CSVs](deliverables/codes/), [audit-report.md](deliverables/audit-report.md) and [audit-questions.md](deliverables/audit-questions.md). The report shows the allocation against the employer's split, each adjustment to the cent with its records, an employee-by-employee basis, facts kept apart from open items, and which employers to call first.

## Do I accept each employer's split?
| Employer | Split | What the decision rests on |
|---|---|---|
| Harbor Point Legal | **Accept** | Register and field notes show all office work. Tomas Reyes's 6 condominium sign-ins are an open item. |
| Larkspur Lane Bistro | **Accept** | Field notes put the catering crew under the caterer code. Their restaurant shifts have no time record (open item). Gross receipts were not used. |
| Bay Crest Exteriors | **Reject** | Crew timesheets show 8 field workers, not 3. Owen Petrakis, titled "Roofer", logged mostly siding hours, so he moves to the siding code. The estimator has 9 site days and moves out of clerical. 319,158.10 leaves C-110. |
| Patuxent Electric | **Reject** | The owner isn't excluded and does field work (214 site days), so he is counted at the flat 63,700.00 under E-510 instead of 118,000.00 under clerical. Travel allowance above 47.00 a day adds 2,550.00 of payroll. |
| Severn Homebuilders | **Reject** | The office manager has 11 site days, so she moves to H-420. Tidewater Drywall has no certificate, and Kent Island's certificate lapsed on 2026-01-31; 60% of those payments adds 43,680.78. |
| Annapolis Courier | **Reject** | The route log shows both dispatchers rode along, so 30,078.05 of their pay moves to the courier code by whole weeks. |

**Call first:** Bay Crest Exteriors, then Patuxent Electric. The ranking is by how much payroll the records move away from the employer's split; that rule is mine. Severn Homebuilders is close behind (163k against Patuxent's 184k) and depends most on documents the employer has to send.

## Not yet confirmed
- The six readings of house practice (A1 to A6) are my interpretation and need Nadia's confirmation.
- The code I gave Teresa Lindqvist (Bay Crest estimator) and Dana Whitcomb (Severn office manager) after they passed the five-day site test is a proposal.
- The employer's per-person split is inferred from the application totals. It came out unique for all six employers, but it is still an inference.

## Missing information for the next interview
1. **Code after the clerical test.** Which code replaces C-110 once a clerical person reaches five or more job-site days. Also whether client sites, closings or errand stops count as "job sites", and whether the five days count across the whole audit period.
2. **Meaning of "by whole weeks"** for dispatcher ride-alongs. I assumed one ride-along day sends that whole week's pay to the courier code.
3. **Mixed crew work.** How to pick the single code when timesheets show more than one kind of work. I used the code with the most hours. Also whether the guide's CG-07 division of payroll is ever allowed.
4. **Owner flat amount details.** Which code it goes under, and whether it applies whatever the owner's actual pay (it lowers Patuxent's payroll) and for a partial year.
5. **Subcontractor coverage.** Whether a certificate is matched to the payment date or the work date, and how to treat a name mismatch on a certificate (Kent Island Roofing against "Kent Island Roofing & Siding LLC").
6. **Allowance with no travel days.** How to treat an allowance paid with zero recorded travel days (Kyle Brandt, 390.00), and how her 47.00 cap relates to the guide's exclusion for documented reimbursements.
7. **Supervisors and temporary workers.** She has no rule yet, and working foremen exist: Darnell Price at Bay Crest and Garrett Holm at Severn.
8. **Restaurant shifts by caterers.** Whether a catering crew's restaurant shifts change their code, and whether receipts ever matter.
9. **Doubtful records.** How to treat entries that look wrong, such as Teresa Lindqvist's sign-in on 2025-12-25. That one day decides her code.
10. **Rule sources.** Confirmation that the CG-nn numbers are the references to cite, and that the July 2025 edition covers the whole audit period. She also said the audit period is in the payroll register; it is actually in the business description.
11. **Call-first criteria.** What she weighs when choosing which two employers to call before Friday.

Context: the first version of insurance-01 is built and has outputs for all six employers. I have now completed teh second interview and placed the transcript in the interviews folder. The previous review identified unresolved interpretations in classification, payroll allocation, soure precedence, and employer follow up.

Instructions: Read the repo guidance, assignment requirements, both interview transcripts, and the current skill and deliverables. Keep both original interview exports complete and unchanged. Update the skill and its supporting references using the second interview answers. Apply only what Nadia confirmed. Don't turn unanswered questions or your own interpretations into company rules. Re run the skill on all six employers using the authoritative sources, and update the required csvs, audit report, and audit questions. Keep the code reusable: don't hard code employer answers.

Expertise and output: Work like a careful premium audit analyst. Separate confirmed rules, source backed facts, and unresolved judgements. Show each payroll adjustment with employee or payment, amount to the cent, supporting records, and applicable compan rule reference. Keep csv columns and paths exactly as the assignment requires, with no zero-payroll rows. The skill classifies and allocates payroll only, it does not set rates or quote premiums.

Verification: Run the relevant tests and output validator. Check that every allocation reconciles, each cited record and rule exists, and unresolved cases remain visible for human review. Confirm the second transcript is inclueded and unchanged and coding session evidence covers the final revision. Report what you ran and anything you could not verify.

Keep the change focused, protect any secrets, do not deploy or push, but add and commit after each coherent addition. Then summarize the decisions changed, remaining information gaps (do not give me in the form of questions), and verification results. Also keep in mind that I am only allowed one more interview, so keep that option as a last resort if there is something super critical we need to know, or you are confident that we will not have any more gaps after this interview.

# Linden Shore Mutual premium audit house practice

The written rules are the classification guide excerpt (paragraphs `CG-nn`), which is the authoritative version of the
rules (interview 1, 08:41 PM). This file records the audit team's unwritten house practice as Nadia Brennan, Senior
Premium Auditor, stated it:

- interview 1: `interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261027-0049.md`, cited as I1
- interview 2: `interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261027-0157.md`, cited as I2

The `HP-n` labels are this Skill's own labels for traceability, not company identifiers. They never go in the
`rationale_ref` column, which takes only the guide's `CG-nn` identifiers. The guide itself says a class code is cited by
the paragraph that describes it.

This file has three parts, and they are kept apart on purpose:

1. **Confirmed rules**: what Nadia stated. Applied as rules.
2. **Stated gaps**: where Nadia said she has no rule or practice. Never filled in as if they were company rules.
3. **Readings**: this Skill's own interpretation where an answer leaves a detail open. Each one is raised as an open
   item wherever it affects an allocation.

## 1. Confirmed rules

| Label | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| HP-1 | Classify people by what they actually do, not by job titles or application estimates. | I1 08:43 PM; I2 09:52 PM, 09:54 PM |
| HP-2 | One person's pay is not split between codes. The only exception is an inside employee (for example a dispatcher) who rides on delivery routes. If they ride on **two or more days in the same Monday-to-Sunday pay week**, that whole week's pay is driver payroll under T-610. A week with only one ride day stays under the employee's own code (C-110 for a dispatcher) in full, the same as a week with no ride. | I1 08:44 PM; I2 09:49 PM, 09:50 PM |
| HP-3 | A working owner who does any field work is counted at a flat **USD 63,700** of payroll under the employer's trade code, regardless of actual wages or what the owner drew. An owner who never works in the field is counted under C-110. | I1 08:44 PM; I2 09:50 PM, 09:51 PM |
| HP-4 | Clerical staff are C-110 unless they are on a job site **five or more days**. Days are counted across the entire audit period from the **site sign-in log**. A clerical person who reaches five days has their **whole payroll moved to the employer's governing code: the field code carrying the most payroll at that employer**. | I1 08:44 PM; I2 09:48 PM |
| HP-5 | Payments to uninsured subcontractors are added to payroll at **60%** of the amount paid, under the code for the work. A certificate of insurance counts only if it covers **the whole audit period** during which the work was performed. | I1 08:44 PM; I2 09:51 PM |
| HP-6 | Daily out-of-town allowances are left out of payroll up to **USD 47 per worker per day**. Any amount above that daily limit is payroll under that worker's code. | I1 08:44 PM; I2 09:52 PM |
| HP-7 | The records in the file decide the allocation. Any difference from what the employer reported goes on that employer's question list for the employer to confirm. | I1 08:45 PM; I2 09:54 PM, 09:55 PM |
| HP-8 | For each discrepancy, record the specific payment or value found in the records and the exact document or log that is the evidence. | I1 08:46 PM |
| HP-9 | Every adjustment, and the record each decision rests on, goes on the question list. A question is actionable if it names the person, days or payment, and the document needed to confirm it. | I1 08:47 PM |
| HP-10 | A case house practice does not cover: propose a treatment, write down why, and mark it as an open item for the employer to confirm. The auditor reviews the proposals. | I1 08:43 PM, 08:46 PM, 08:47 PM; I2 09:51 PM, 09:56 PM |
| HP-11 | Process each employer individually. The auditor reviews the results and the proposed gray-area handling before they count as audit work. | I1 08:48 PM, 08:49 PM |
| HP-12 | Underwriting sends the quotes on Friday and the auditor can call only two employers before then. Which two is the analyst's call, with reasons. | I1 08:47 PM; I2 09:55 PM |
| HP-13 | Tests are applied in **days, not hours**. The specific test depends on the record: sign-in logs, route logs or crew timesheets. | I2 09:49 PM |
| HP-14 | The caterer code F-720 applies only if off-site catering is **40% or more of the employer's gross receipts**. Below that, the catering crew stays under the restaurant code F-710. | I2 09:52 PM, 09:53 PM |
| HP-15 | A record that looks questionable (for example a sign-in on a holiday) is used as written to decide the allocation, and is added to the question list for the employer to confirm. | I2 09:53 PM |

## 2. Stated gaps (no rule exists; never written up as one)

| Gap | Source | How the Skill handles it |
|---|---|---|
| Supervisors, foremen, temporary workers: no specific rules; classify by actual duties (HP-1). | I1 08:44 PM; I2 09:52 PM | Classified by duties like anyone else. |
| Owner who worked only part of the audit period. | I2 09:51 PM | Open item if a record shows it. |
| Allowance paid with no travel days recorded. Nadia said to allocate under practice and the guide as they stand, and to write down how and why. | I2 09:51 PM | Reading R6. |
| Certificate issued in a name that differs from the payee. | I2 09:51 PM | Open item, with whether it changes the allocation. |
| Which source is authoritative if the business description and payroll register disagree on the audit period. | I2 09:55 PM | Period read from the file that states it; open item if two files disagree. |
| Whether the July 2025 guide edition covers the whole audit period. Nadia knows only the guide she has. | I2 09:54 PM | The guide at the source location is used and its edition and hash are printed. |
| How to choose a single code for a crew member whose timesheets show more than one kind of work. HP-13 says use days, but the timesheet test itself was not stated. | I2 09:49 PM | Reading R2. |

## 3. Readings (the Skill's interpretation; always raised as an open item where they matter)

- **R2 (crew timesheets, HP-2 and HP-13).** A crew member with more than one kind of work recorded is reported wholly
  under the code with the **most recorded days**. A tie is an open item.
- **R4 (governing code, HP-4).** The governing code is computed from employees' payroll under codes other than C-110,
  before any clerical person is moved, after the caterer receipts test, and without subcontractor additions. If counting
  subcontractor additions would pick a different code, that is raised as an open item. If the employer has no field
  code at all, the rule cannot apply: the person stays C-110 and an open item is raised.
- **R3 (owner's trade code, HP-3).** The worksheet names the owner's trade code from the records. If it differs from
  the governing code, that is raised as an open item.
- **R6 (allowance with no travel days).** With no recorded travel days, nothing qualifies for the USD 47 per-day
  exclusion (HP-6 as it stands), so the whole allowance is payroll under the worker's code.
- **R14 (receipts period).** The receipts test (HP-14) uses every month in the receipts record that overlaps the audit
  period. When the months do not line up exactly with the audit period, the report says so and shows the share.

"""Apply the classification guide and the audit team's confirmed house practice to one employer's records.

The worksheet (written per employer by the analyst running the Skill) supplies the judgments the records cannot make on
their own: the code that describes each person's actual duties, which code each type of crew work and subcontracted
trade falls under, owner status, and which receipts columns are off-site catering. Everything that is arithmetic or a
confirmed house rule (references/house-practice.md, HP-n) is applied here, from the records, the same way for every
employer. Where a rule leaves a detail open, the Skill's reading (R-n) is applied and raised as an open item.
"""

import datetime
import itertools
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

from .records import CENT, day, money

FIXED_HOLIDAYS = {(1, 1): "New Year's Day", (7, 4): "Independence Day", (12, 25): "Christmas Day"}
ZERO = Decimal("0.00")


class WorksheetError(ValueError):
    pass


@dataclass
class Line:
    code: str
    amount: Decimal
    basis: str


@dataclass
class Person:
    id: str
    name: str
    position: str
    wages: Decimal
    lines: list = field(default_factory=list)
    records: list = field(default_factory=list)
    employer_code: str | None = None
    evidence: str = ""  # plain statement of the time records, worded for the employer question list

    @property
    def primary_code(self):
        return max(self.lines, key=lambda l: l.amount).code


@dataclass
class Adjustment:
    about: str
    kind: str
    amount: Decimal
    code: str
    detail: str
    records: list
    rule: str


@dataclass
class OpenItem:
    about: str
    proposal: str
    why: str
    records: list
    rule: str = "HP-10"
    question: str = ""  # the employer question that would settle it (HP-10: open item for the employer to confirm)


@dataclass
class Result:
    rec: dict
    ws: dict
    people: list = field(default_factory=list)
    sub_lines: list = field(default_factory=list)
    adjustments: list = field(default_factory=list)
    open_items: list = field(default_factory=list)
    questionable: list = field(default_factory=list)  # (about, record, detail): used as written, sent to the employer
    questions: list = field(default_factory=list)
    notes: list = field(default_factory=list)
    applied: list = field(default_factory=list)  # confirmed rules (HP-n) that changed or decided something
    totals: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    governing_code: str | None = None
    reconciliation: list = field(default_factory=list)
    inference: str = ""

    @property
    def employer_split(self):
        return {c: v["payroll"] for c, v in self.rec["employer_split"].items()}

    def differences(self):
        codes = sorted(set(self.totals) | set(self.employer_split))
        return {c: self.totals.get(c, ZERO) - self.employer_split.get(c, ZERO) for c in codes}

    @property
    def accepts_employer_split(self):
        return all(d == 0 for d in self.differences().values()) and not any(
            p.employer_code and {l.code for l in p.lines} != {p.employer_code} for p in self.people)


def _uniq(items):
    return list(dict.fromkeys(i for i in items if i))


def fmt(amount):
    return f"{amount:,.2f}"


def infer_employer_codes(register, split):
    """Find the one assignment of register employees to the employer's codes that reproduces its split.

    The application gives only a head count and payroll per code. The pairing is used only to explain where the first
    pass differs from the employer; it never decides a classification (HP-1: not by application estimates).
    """
    codes = list(split)
    if len(codes) ** len(register) > 3_000_000:
        return None, "too many employees to pair the employer's split with people; it is compared by code only"
    hits = []
    for combo in itertools.product(codes, repeat=len(register)):
        counts, sums = Counter(combo), defaultdict(Decimal)
        if any(counts[c] != split[c]["employees"] for c in codes):
            continue
        for code, e in zip(combo, register):
            sums[code] += e["wages"]
        if all(sums[c] == split[c]["payroll"] for c in codes):
            hits.append(dict(zip((e["id"] for e in register), combo)))
            if len(hits) > 1:
                return None, "more than one pairing of people fits the employer's split; it is compared by code only"
    if not hits:
        return None, "no pairing of register wages reproduces the employer's split exactly; it is compared by code only"
    return hits[0], ("the application names no people; exactly one pairing of register wages reproduces its head count "
                     "and payroll for every code, so 'Employer's code' shows that pairing. It explains differences "
                     "only and decided no classification (HP-1)")


def allocate(guide, hp, rec, ws):
    res = Result(rec, ws)
    clerical = hp["clerical_code"]
    threshold = int(hp["clerical_job_site_day_threshold"])
    min_ride = int(hp["route_split_min_ride_days_per_week"])
    owner_flat = money(hp["owner_field_work_flat_payroll"])
    start, end = rec["period"]
    in_period = lambda d: start <= d <= end  # noqa: E731
    reg_file = rec["register_file"]

    def code_ok(code, where):
        if not code:
            raise WorksheetError(f"{where} is not filled in; decide it from the records (see SKILL.md, step 3)")
        try:
            guide.ref_for(code)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise WorksheetError(f"{where}: {exc}") from None
        return code

    def applied(rule):
        if rule not in res.applied:
            res.applied.append(rule)

    ws_people = ws.get("employees", {})
    missing = [e["id"] for e in rec["register"] if e["id"] not in ws_people]
    extra = [i for i in ws_people if i not in {e["id"] for e in rec["register"]}]
    if missing or extra:
        raise WorksheetError(f"worksheet employees do not match {reg_file}: missing {missing or 'none'}, "
                             f"not on register {extra or 'none'}")

    def out_of_period(rows, key, file):
        n = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get(key) and not in_period(day(r[key])))
        if n:
            res.notes.append(f"{n} row(s) in {file} fall outside the audit period and were not used.")

    # Index the supporting records, audit period only.
    timesheets = defaultdict(list)
    for r in rec["timesheets"]:
        if in_period(day(r["date"])):
            timesheets[r["employee_id"]].append(r)
    out_of_period(rec["timesheets"], "date", rec["timesheets_file"])

    site_days = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(set))
    for r in rec["signins"]:
        if r["employee_id"] and in_period(day(r["date"])):
            site_days[r["employee_id"]][day(r["date"])].add(r["site"])
    others = [r for r in rec["signins"] if not r["employee_id"]]
    if others:
        res.notes.append(f"{len(others)} sign-in row(s) in {rec['signins_file']} have no employee ID "
                         f"({', '.join(sorted({r.get('name', '?') for r in others}))}); they are not employees and were not used.")
    out_of_period(rec["signins"], "date", rec["signins_file"])

    ride_days = defaultdict(set)
    for r in rec["route_log"]:
        if r["ride_along_id"] and in_period(day(r["date"])):
            ride_days[r["ride_along_id"]].add(day(r["date"]))
    out_of_period(rec["route_log"], "date", rec["route_log_file"])

    weekly = defaultdict(list)
    for r in rec["weekly_payroll"]:
        weekly[r["employee_id"]].append((day(r["week_start"]), day(r["week_end"]), money(r["gross_pay"])))

    work_codes = ws.get("work_type_codes", {})
    route_code = ws.get("route_code") and code_ok(ws["route_code"], "route_code")
    if ride_days and not route_code:
        raise WorksheetError(f"{rec['route_log_file']} records ride-alongs, but worksheet route_code is not filled in")
    split_people, pending, owners = [], [], []

    # Pass 1: each person's own code from duties and time records.
    for e in rec["register"]:
        w = ws_people[e["id"]]
        duty = code_ok(w.get("duty_code") or "", f"employees.{e['id']}.duty_code")
        p = Person(e["id"], e["name"], e["position"], e["wages"], records=[reg_file] + w.get("records", []))
        owner = ws.get("owners", {}).get(e["id"])

        if owner and owner.get("included"):
            p.records = _uniq(p.records + owner.get("records", []))
            if owner.get("field_work"):
                code = code_ok(owner.get("field_code") or duty, f"owners.{e['id']}.field_code")
                p.lines = [Line(code, owner_flat, f"Working owner who does field work ({owner['basis']}). Counted at the "
                                                  f"flat {fmt(owner_flat)}, regardless of actual wages, under the "
                                                  f"employer's trade code {code} (HP-3).")]
                res.adjustments.append(Adjustment(
                    e["name"], "Owner counted at flat amount", owner_flat, code,
                    f"{reg_file} shows wages of {fmt(e['wages'])}. A working owner who does any field work is counted "
                    f"at {fmt(owner_flat)} regardless of actual wages, under the employer's trade code {code} "
                    f"(difference {fmt(owner_flat - e['wages'])}).", _uniq(p.records), "HP-3"))
                owners.append(p)
                applied("HP-3")
            else:
                p.lines = [Line(clerical, e["wages"], f"Owner who never works in the field: {clerical} (HP-3). "
                                                      f"Counted at register wages (reading R3).")]
                res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                    e["name"], f"Count {e['name']} at the register wages of {fmt(e['wages'])} under {clerical}.",
                    f"House practice puts an owner who never works in the field under {clerical} but does not state the "
                    f"amount. The register wages are the only record of it.", [reg_file] + owner.get("records", []),
                    "HP-3, R3",
                    f"{e['name']} ({reg_file}): please confirm that {e['name']} did no field work in the audit period "
                    f"and the {fmt(e['wages'])} of pay shown in {reg_file}."))
            res.people.append(p)
            continue

        final, basis = duty, w["basis"]
        rows = timesheets.get(e["id"])
        if rows:
            by_code, by_type = defaultdict(set), defaultdict(set)
            for r in rows:
                if r["work_type"] not in work_codes:
                    raise WorksheetError(f"work type {r['work_type']!r} in {rec['timesheets_file']} has no entry in "
                                         f"worksheet work_type_codes")
                code = code_ok(work_codes[r["work_type"]], f"work_type_codes.{r['work_type']}")
                by_code[code].add(r["date"])
                by_type[r["work_type"]].add(r["date"])
            days_by_code = {c: len(d) for c, d in by_code.items()}
            ranked = sorted(days_by_code.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])
            leaders = [c for c, n in ranked if n == ranked[0][1]]
            final = duty if duty in leaders else leaders[0]
            mix = ", ".join(f"{t} {len(d)} days" for t, d in sorted(by_type.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])))
            basis = (f"{rec['timesheets_file']}: {mix}. One person's pay is not split (HP-2) and tests are in days "
                     f"(HP-13); the whole pay goes to {final}, the code with the most recorded days (reading R2).")
            p.records.append(rec["timesheets_file"])
            p.evidence = f"{rec['timesheets_file']} records {mix} for {e['name']}."
            applied("HP-13")
            if len(days_by_code) > 1:
                split_people.append((p, days_by_code, final))
            if len(leaders) > 1:
                res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                    e["name"], f"Report all of {e['name']}'s pay under {final}.",
                    f"The timesheets show equal days under {', '.join(leaders)}, and house practice does not say how "
                    f"to break a tie.", [rec["timesheets_file"]], "HP-10, R2",
                    f"{e['name']} ({rec['timesheets_file']}): {p.evidence} Please confirm which work {e['name']} "
                    f"mainly did during the audit period."))
        elif duty == clerical and site_days.get(e["id"]):
            days = site_days[e["id"]]
            p.records.append(rec["signins_file"])
            dates = ", ".join(d.isoformat() for d in sorted(days))
            p.evidence = (f"{rec['signins_file']} records {e['name']} at a job site on {len(days)} day(s): " + "; ".join(
                f"{d.isoformat()} {', '.join(sorted(days[d]))}" for d in sorted(days)) + ".")
            for d in sorted(days):
                if (d.month, d.day) in FIXED_HOLIDAYS:
                    res.questionable.append((e["name"], rec["signins_file"],
                                             f"{rec['signins_file']} records {e['name']} at {', '.join(sorted(days[d]))} "
                                             f"on {d.isoformat()} ({FIXED_HOLIDAYS[(d.month, d.day)]})"))
                    applied("HP-15")
            if len(days) < threshold:
                basis += (f" {rec['signins_file']} shows {len(days)} job-site day(s) in the audit period ({dates}), "
                          f"fewer than {threshold}, so the person stays {clerical} (HP-4).")
                applied("HP-4")
            else:
                pending.append((p, w, days, dates))
        p.lines = [Line(final, e["wages"], basis)]

        rides = ride_days.get(e["id"])
        if route_code and rides and final != route_code:
            weeks = sorted(weekly.get(e["id"], []))
            p.records += [rec["route_log_file"]]
            if not weeks:
                res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                    e["name"], f"Leave all of {e['name']}'s pay under {final}.",
                    f"{rec['route_log_file']} shows {len(rides)} ride-along days, but there is no weekly pay record, so "
                    f"the whole-week test (HP-2) cannot be applied.", [rec["route_log_file"]], "HP-2, HP-10",
                    f"{e['name']} ({rec['route_log_file']}): please send {e['name']}'s weekly gross pay for the audit "
                    f"period, Monday to Sunday."))
            else:
                p.records.append(rec["weekly_payroll_file"])
                per_week = [(s, t, g, sum(1 for d in rides if s <= d <= t)) for s, t, g in weeks]
                hist = Counter(n for *_, n in per_week)
                moved_weeks = [w_ for w_ in per_week if w_[3] >= min_ride]
                moved = sum((g for _, _, g, _ in moved_weeks), ZERO)
                weekly_total = sum((g for _, _, g in weeks), ZERO)
                if weekly_total != e["wages"]:
                    res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                        e["name"], f"Use {reg_file} for the total and {rec['weekly_payroll_file']} for the week split.",
                        f"The weekly pay totals {fmt(weekly_total)} but {reg_file} shows {fmt(e['wages'])}.",
                        [reg_file, rec["weekly_payroll_file"]], "HP-10",
                        f"{e['name']} ({reg_file}, {rec['weekly_payroll_file']}): the weekly pay totals "
                        f"{fmt(weekly_total)} but the register shows {fmt(e['wages'])}; please send the reconciliation."))
                split_text = (f"{len(rides)} ride-along days in the audit period. Pay weeks by ride days: "
                              + ", ".join(f"{n} day(s) {hist[n]} week(s)" for n in sorted(hist)) + ".")
                applied("HP-2")
                if moved:
                    p.lines = [
                        Line(route_code, moved, f"{rec['route_log_file']}: {split_text} The {len(moved_weeks)} weeks "
                                                f"with {min_ride} or more ride days are driver payroll under "
                                                f"{route_code} (HP-2)."),
                        Line(final, e["wages"] - moved, f"{basis} The other {len(weeks) - len(moved_weeks)} pay weeks "
                                                        f"(no ride day or only one) stay under {final} (HP-2)."),
                    ]
                    res.adjustments.append(Adjustment(
                        e["name"], "Whole-week route split", moved, route_code,
                        f"{split_text} {len(moved_weeks)} pay weeks have {min_ride} or more ride days; their gross pay "
                        f"of {fmt(moved)} moves from {final} to {route_code}: "
                        + ", ".join(f"{s.isoformat()} ({n} days, {fmt(g)})" for s, _, g, n in moved_weeks) + ".",
                        [rec["route_log_file"], rec["weekly_payroll_file"]], "HP-2"))
                else:
                    p.lines[0].basis += (f" {rec['route_log_file']}: {split_text} No pay week has {min_ride} or more "
                                         f"ride days, so all pay stays under {final} (HP-2).")
                p.evidence = (f"{rec['route_log_file']} records {e['name']} as a ride-along on {len(rides)} day(s): "
                              + ", ".join(d.isoformat() for d in sorted(rides)) + ".")

        _travel(res, hp, e, p, reg_file)
        p.records = _uniq(p.records)
        res.people.append(p)

    _caterer_test(res, hp, rec, ws, code_ok)

    # Governing code (HP-4): the field code carrying the most payroll, before any clerical move (reading R4).
    field_pay = defaultdict(Decimal)
    for p in res.people:
        for l in p.lines:
            if l.code != clerical:
                field_pay[l.code] += l.amount
    res.governing_code = max(field_pay, key=field_pay.get) if field_pay else None
    gov_mix = ", ".join(f"{c} {fmt(v)}" for c, v in sorted(field_pay.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])) or "none"

    for p, w, days, dates in pending:
        applied("HP-4")
        if res.governing_code:
            for l in p.lines:
                if l.code == clerical:
                    l.code = res.governing_code
            p.lines[0].basis = (f"{w['basis']} {rec['signins_file']} shows {len(days)} job-site days in the audit "
                                f"period ({dates}): five or more, so the whole payroll moves to the employer's governing "
                                f"code {res.governing_code}, the field code carrying the most payroll ({gov_mix}) (HP-4).")
        else:
            p.lines[0].basis += (f" {rec['signins_file']} shows {len(days)} job-site days ({dates}), five or more, but "
                                 f"the employer has no field code, so there is no governing code to move to.")
            res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                p.name, f"Keep {p.name} under {clerical}.",
                f"{len(days)} job-site days meets the five-day test (HP-4), and the rule moves the whole payroll to the "
                f"field code carrying the most payroll. This employer has no payroll under any field code, so the rule "
                f"has nothing to move to, and the guide has no code for the work recorded at "
                f"{', '.join(sorted({s for v in days.values() for s in v}))}.",
                [rec["signins_file"]] + w.get("records", []), "HP-4, HP-10",
                f"{p.name} ({rec['signins_file']}): {p.evidence} Please describe what {p.name} did at each visit, and "
                f"whether any of it was physical work outside the office."))

    for p in owners:
        if res.governing_code and p.lines[0].code != res.governing_code:
            res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                p.name, f"Keep the owner's flat amount under {p.lines[0].code}.",
                f"House practice counts a working owner under the employer's trade code. The worksheet names "
                f"{p.lines[0].code}, but the field code carrying the most payroll is {res.governing_code}.",
                p.records, "HP-3, R3",
                f"{p.name} ({', '.join(p.records)}): please describe the field work {p.name} did during the audit period."))

    _subcontractors(res, hp, rec, ws, code_ok, in_period)

    if pending and res.governing_code and res.sub_lines:
        with_subs = defaultdict(Decimal, field_pay)
        for l in res.sub_lines:
            with_subs[l.code] += l.amount
        alt = max(with_subs, key=with_subs.get)
        if alt != res.governing_code:
            res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                "Governing code", f"Use {res.governing_code}, from employees' payroll only.",
                f"Counting subcontractor additions would make {alt} the governing code. House practice does not say "
                f"which payroll decides it (reading R4).", [rec["sub_payments_file"]], "HP-4, R4"))

    if split_people:
        rows = "; ".join(f"{p.name}: " + ", ".join(f"{c} {n} days" for c, n in sorted(bc.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))
                         + f", reported under {f}" for p, bc, f in split_people)
        res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
            "Crew members with more than one type of work",
            "Report each person's whole pay under the code with the most recorded days.",
            f"Confirmed: one person's pay is not split except for route ride-alongs (HP-2), and tests use days, not "
            f"hours (HP-13). Not stated: the crew-timesheet test that picks the single code. The most-days choice is "
            f"this Skill's reading (R2). Days by code: {rows}.", [rec["timesheets_file"]], "HP-10, R2"))

    for item in ws.get("open_items", []):
        target = next((o for o in res.open_items if o.about == item.get("merge_with")), None)
        if target:  # the analyst's context for an item the rules already raised
            target.proposal = item.get("proposal", target.proposal)
            target.why += " " + item["why"]
            target.records = _uniq(target.records + item.get("records", []))
            target.question = item.get("employer_question", target.question)
        else:
            res.open_items.append(OpenItem(item["about"], item["proposal"], item["why"], item.get("records", []),
                                           item.get("rule", "HP-10"), item.get("employer_question", "")))

    totals = defaultdict(Decimal)
    for line in [l for p in res.people for l in p.lines] + res.sub_lines:
        totals[line.code] += line.amount
    res.totals = {c: v.quantize(CENT) for c, v in sorted(totals.items()) if v}
    _reconcile(res, rec)

    mapping, res.inference = infer_employer_codes(rec["register"], rec["employer_split"])
    for p in res.people:
        p.employer_code = (mapping or {}).get(p.id)
        if p.employer_code and p.primary_code != p.employer_code and not any(a.about == p.name for a in res.adjustments):
            res.adjustments.append(Adjustment(
                p.name, "Reclassified", p.wages, p.primary_code,
                f"The records put {p.name}'s {fmt(p.wages)} under {p.primary_code}: {p.lines[0].basis} (Employer's "
                f"split pairs {p.name} with {p.employer_code}.)", p.records, "HP-1, HP-7"))
        for a in res.adjustments:
            if a.about == p.name and a.kind != "Reclassified" and p.employer_code and p.employer_code != a.code:
                a.detail += f" (Employer's split pairs {p.name} with {p.employer_code}.)"

    _questions(res, rec, ws)
    return res


def _travel(res, hp, e, p, reg_file):
    if not e["travel_allowance"]:
        return
    cap = money(hp["out_of_town_daily_allowance_exclusion"])
    code = p.lines[-1].code
    tdays = e["travel_days"] or 0
    excluded = min(e["travel_allowance"], cap * tdays)
    excess = e["travel_allowance"] - excluded
    src = f"{reg_file} (travel_days, travel_allowance_paid)"
    p.records.append(src)
    if "HP-6" not in res.applied:
        res.applied.append("HP-6")
    if excess:
        p.lines.append(Line(code, excess, f"Daily allowance above {fmt(cap)} per day: {fmt(e['travel_allowance'])} paid "
                                          f"for {tdays} travel days, {fmt(excluded)} left out (HP-6)."))
        res.adjustments.append(Adjustment(
            e["name"], "Travel allowance above the daily exclusion", excess, code,
            f"{fmt(e['travel_allowance'])} paid for {tdays} recorded travel days. Up to {fmt(cap)} per day "
            f"({fmt(excluded)}) is left out; the remaining {fmt(excess)} is payroll under {code}.", [src],
            "HP-6" if tdays else "HP-6, R6"))
    if tdays == 0:
        res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
            e["name"], f"Count all {fmt(e['travel_allowance'])} of the allowance as payroll under {code}.",
            f"{reg_file} records an allowance but no travel days. Nadia has no practice for this and asked for it to be "
            f"allocated under practice and the guide as they stand. HP-6 leaves out up to {fmt(cap)} per travel day, so "
            f"with no recorded day nothing qualifies, and the amount is payroll (reading R6).", [reg_file], "HP-6, R6"))


def _caterer_test(res, hp, rec, ws, code_ok):
    """HP-14: the caterer code applies only if off-site catering is 40% or more of the employer's gross receipts."""
    caterer, restaurant = hp["caterer_code"], hp["restaurant_code"]
    crew = [p for p in res.people if any(l.code == caterer for l in p.lines)]
    if not crew:
        return
    cfg = ws.get("receipts") or {}
    name = cfg.get("file") or rec.get("receipts_file")
    names = ", ".join(p.name for p in crew)
    if not name or not cfg.get("offsite_columns") or not cfg.get("other_columns"):
        res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
            f"Caterer receipts test ({names})", f"Keep {names} under {caterer} until the receipts test can be run.",
            f"{caterer} applies only if off-site catering is {Decimal(hp['caterer_min_offsite_receipts_share']):.0%} or "
            f"more of gross receipts (HP-14), and the file has no receipts record mapped in the worksheet.", [],
            "HP-14, HP-10", f"{names}: please send monthly gross receipts for the audit period, split between off-site "
                            f"catering and everything else."))
        return
    rows = rec["file"].rows(name, ["month"] + cfg["offsite_columns"] + cfg["other_columns"])
    start, end = rec["period"]
    used, partial = [], []
    for r in rows:
        first = datetime.date.fromisoformat(r["month"] + "-01")
        last = (first.replace(day=28) + datetime.timedelta(days=4)).replace(day=1) - datetime.timedelta(days=1)
        if first <= end and last >= start:
            used.append(r)
            if first < start or last > end:
                partial.append(r["month"])
    offsite = sum((money(r[c]) for r in used for c in cfg["offsite_columns"]), ZERO)
    total = offsite + sum((money(r[c]) for r in used for c in cfg["other_columns"]), ZERO)
    share = offsite / total if total else Decimal(0)
    need = Decimal(hp["caterer_min_offsite_receipts_share"])
    months = f"{used[0]['month']} to {used[-1]['month']}" if used else "none"
    text = (f"{name}, {months}: off-site catering {fmt(offsite)} of {fmt(total)} gross receipts = {share:.2%} "
            f"(test: {need:.0%} or more for {caterer}, HP-14).")
    if partial:
        res.notes.append(f"{name}: months {', '.join(partial)} only partly overlap the audit period "
                         f"{start.isoformat()} to {end.isoformat()} and were counted whole (reading R14).")
    res.applied.append("HP-14")
    res.notes.append(f"Caterer receipts test: {text}")
    for p in crew:
        p.records = _uniq(p.records + [name])
        if share < need:
            moved = sum((l.amount for l in p.lines if l.code == caterer), ZERO)
            for l in p.lines:
                if l.code == caterer:
                    l.code = restaurant
            p.lines[0].basis += f" {text} Below the test, so the catering crew stays under {restaurant}."
            res.adjustments.append(Adjustment(
                p.name, "Caterer receipts test", moved, restaurant,
                f"{p.name} works on the catering crew. {text} Below {need:.0%}, so {fmt(moved)} goes under {restaurant}, "
                f"not {caterer}.", [name] + [r for r in p.records if r != name], "HP-14"))
        else:
            p.lines[0].basis += f" {text} At or above the test, so {caterer} applies."
    code_ok(restaurant, "house_practice.restaurant_code")


def _subcontractors(res, hp, rec, ws, code_ok, in_period):
    if not rec["sub_payments"]:
        return
    share = Decimal(hp["uninsured_subcontractor_payroll_share"])
    start, end = rec["period"]
    certs = defaultdict(list)
    for c in rec["certificates"]:
        certs[c["subcontractor"]].append((c["certificate_no"], day(c["coverage_from"]), day(c["coverage_to"])))
    matches = ws.get("subcontractor_certificate_matches", {})
    work_codes = ws.get("subcontract_work_codes", {})
    files = _uniq([rec["sub_payments_file"], rec["certificates_file"]])
    by_sub = defaultdict(list)
    for pay in rec["sub_payments"]:
        if in_period(day(pay["date"])):
            by_sub[pay["subcontractor"]].append(pay)
        else:
            res.notes.append(f"{pay['subcontractor']} invoice {pay.get('invoice', '?')} ({pay['date']}, "
                             f"{fmt(money(pay['amount_paid']))}) in {rec['sub_payments_file']} falls outside the audit "
                             f"period and was not used.")
    res.applied.append("HP-5")
    period = f"{start.isoformat()} to {end.isoformat()}"
    for sub, pays in by_sub.items():
        cert_name = sub if sub in certs else matches.get(sub)
        held = certs.get(cert_name, [])
        whole = [c for c in held if c[1] <= start and c[2] >= end]
        if cert_name and cert_name != sub:
            effect = ("This decides whether the payments are insured." if whole else
                      "It does not change the allocation: that certificate does not cover the whole audit period, so "
                      "the payments are added either way.")
            res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                sub, f"Treat the certificate issued to '{cert_name}' as {sub}'s.",
                f"{rec['sub_payments_file']} pays '{sub}', but the certificate in {rec['certificates_file']} is issued to "
                f"'{cert_name}'. Nadia has no practice for a name that differs. {effect}", files, "HP-10",
                f"{sub} ({', '.join(files)}): please confirm whether '{sub}' and '{cert_name}' are the same business, "
                f"with its legal name and federal tax ID."))
        listing = ", ".join(f"{p.get('invoice', '?')} ({p['date']}, {fmt(money(p['amount_paid']))})" for p in pays)
        lead = f"{sub} ({', '.join(files)})"
        if whole:
            res.notes.append(f"{sub}: certificate {whole[0][0]} covers the whole audit period ({period}); "
                             f"{len(pays)} payment(s) not added to payroll (HP-5).")
            res.questions.append((sub, f"{lead}: please confirm that certificate {whole[0][0]} covered {sub}'s own "
                                       f"workers for the whole audit period {period}, including invoices {listing}."))
            continue
        why = ("no certificate of insurance for this subcontractor is in the file" if not held else
               "the certificate in the file (" + "; ".join(f"{n}, {f.isoformat()} to {t.isoformat()}" for n, f, t in held)
               + f") does not cover the whole audit period {period}")
        for pay in pays:
            work = pay["work"]
            if work not in work_codes:
                raise WorksheetError(f"subcontracted work {work!r} has no entry in worksheet subcontract_work_codes")
            code = code_ok(work_codes[work], f"subcontract_work_codes.{work}")
            paid = money(pay["amount_paid"])
            added = (paid * share).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
            res.sub_lines.append(Line(code, added, f"{share:.0%} of {fmt(paid)} paid to uninsured subcontractor {sub} "
                                                   f"(invoice {pay.get('invoice', '?')}, {pay['date']}, {work}) (HP-5, CG-06)."))
            res.adjustments.append(Adjustment(
                f"{sub}, invoice {pay.get('invoice', '?')}", "Uninsured subcontractor payment added", added, code,
                f"{fmt(paid)} paid on {pay['date']} for {work}. Because {why}, {share:.0%} ({fmt(added)}) is added to "
                f"payroll under {code}, the code for the work.", files, "HP-5, CG-06"))
        res.notes.append(f"{sub}: {why}; all {len(pays)} payment(s) added at {share:.0%} (HP-5).")
        res.questions.append((sub, f"{lead}: {why}. Please send a workers' compensation certificate covering {sub}'s "
                                   f"own workers for the whole audit period {period}. Without one, {share:.0%} of "
                                   f"invoices {listing} stays in payroll."))


def _reconcile(res, rec):
    """Register wages plus every adjustment that adds or removes payroll must equal the allocated total."""
    register = sum((e["wages"] for e in rec["register"]), ZERO)
    steps = [("Payroll register wages", register)]
    for a in res.adjustments:
        if a.kind == "Owner counted at flat amount":
            p = next(p for p in res.people if p.name == a.about)
            steps.append((f"{a.about}: flat {fmt(a.amount)} replaces register wages {fmt(p.wages)}", a.amount - p.wages))
        elif a.kind in ("Travel allowance above the daily exclusion", "Uninsured subcontractor payment added"):
            steps.append((f"{a.about}: {a.kind.lower()}", a.amount))
    total = sum((v for _, v in steps), ZERO)
    allocated = sum(res.totals.values(), ZERO)
    if total != allocated:
        raise AssertionError(f"reconciliation failed: register plus adjustments {total} != allocated {allocated}")
    res.reconciliation = steps + [("First-pass total (equals the sum of the codes CSV)", allocated)]


def _questions(res, rec, ws):
    """Every adjustment, every record a decision rests on, every questionable record and every open item gets at least
    one employer question (HP-9, HP-10, HP-15)."""
    reg = rec["register_file"]
    adjusted = {a.about for a in res.adjustments}
    sub_qs = list(res.questions)
    res.questions = []
    q = lambda about, text: res.questions.append((about, text))  # noqa: E731

    for a in res.adjustments:
        if a.kind == "Uninsured subcontractor payment added":
            continue
        p = next((p for p in res.people if p.name == a.about), None)
        if a.kind == "Owner counted at flat amount":
            q(a.about, f"{a.about} ({', '.join(p.records)}): please confirm that {a.about} has not filed an election "
                       f"of exclusion, did field work during the audit period, and was paid the {fmt(p.wages)} shown in "
                       f"{reg}.")
        elif a.kind == "Whole-week route split":
            q(a.about, f"{a.about} ({rec['route_log_file']}, {rec['weekly_payroll_file']}): {p.evidence} Please confirm "
                       f"these ride-along days and the weekly gross pay in the weeks with two or more of them "
                       f"(total {fmt(a.amount)}).")
        elif a.kind == "Travel allowance above the daily exclusion":
            row = next(e for e in rec["register"] if e["name"] == a.about)
            if row["travel_days"]:
                q(a.about, f"{a.about} ({reg}, travel columns): please confirm the {row['travel_days']} out-of-town "
                           f"travel days and the {fmt(row['travel_allowance'])} daily allowance paid, with the trip dates "
                           f"and job.")
            else:
                q(a.about, f"{a.about} ({reg}, travel columns): the register shows a {fmt(row['travel_allowance'])} "
                           f"travel allowance but no travel days. Please say what the payment was for and, if it was "
                           f"for out-of-town work, send the dates and job.")
        elif a.kind == "Caterer receipts test":
            q(a.about, f"{a.about} ({', '.join(a.records)}): please confirm the monthly split of gross receipts between "
                       f"off-site catering and the restaurant for the audit period, and that {a.about} worked on the "
                       f"catering crew.")
        elif a.kind == "Reclassified":
            recs = ", ".join(r for r in p.records if r != reg)
            q(a.about, f"{a.about} ({recs or reg}): {p.evidence or 'The records in the file describe other work.'} "
                       f"Please confirm {a.about}'s actual duties during the audit period and that these records are "
                       f"complete.")

    for p in res.people:
        if p.name in adjusted:
            continue
        if p.evidence:
            q(p.name, f"{p.name} ({', '.join(r for r in p.records if r != reg)}): {p.evidence} Please confirm that "
                      f"these records are complete and correct for the audit period.")
        travel = next((e for e in rec["register"] if e["id"] == p.id and e["travel_allowance"]), None)
        if travel:
            q(p.name, f"{p.name} ({reg}, travel columns): please confirm the {travel['travel_days']} travel days and the "
                      f"{fmt(travel['travel_allowance'])} allowance paid.")

    for about, record, detail in res.questionable:
        q(about, f"{about} ({record}): {detail}. The first pass uses the record as written. Please confirm it or send "
                 f"the corrected record.")

    if res.people:
        listing = "; ".join(f"{p.name}, {p.position}, {fmt(p.wages)} (first pass: "
                            + ", ".join(f"{fmt(l.amount)} {l.code}" for l in p.lines) + ")" for p in res.people)
        q("Payroll register", f"{reg}: please confirm that these wages are complete for the audit period "
                              f"{rec['period'][0].isoformat()} to {rec['period'][1].isoformat()}, and that each "
                              f"person's work matches the code given: {listing}.")

    res.questions += sub_qs
    for c in ws.get("confirmations", []):
        q(c["about"], c["question"])
    asked = " ".join(t for _, t in res.questions)
    for o in res.open_items:
        if o.question:
            q(o.about, o.question)
        elif not any(r and r in asked for r in o.records) or o.about not in asked:
            q(o.about, f"{o.about} ({', '.join(o.records) or 'records in the file'}): the first pass proposes: "
                       f"{o.proposal} Please confirm, or send the record that shows otherwise.")

content.text:
I updated the Skill with interview 2, re-ran it on all six employers from the Drive sources, and committed everything; nothing was pushed. The tests pass (14), the validator passes (270 of 270), and every employer's allocation reconciles to the cent. Both interview exports are committed and unchanged.

## Decisions that changed
| Employer | Before | Now | Why (Nadia, interview 2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Larkspur Lane Bistro | Accepted (catering crew under F-720) | **Not accepted:** all 340,725.35 under F-710 | Caterer code needs off-site catering at 40% or more of receipts. The receipts file shows 22.00%. |
| Annapolis Courier | 30,078.05 moved to T-610 | **22,808.75** moved, from Lena Ortiz only | Only pay weeks with two or more ride days move. Lena has 25 such weeks; Paul's two ride days fall in separate weeks, so he stays C-110. |
| Severn Homebuilders | R-310 18,987.39 | **R-310 27,567.39** | A certificate must cover the whole audit period. Kent Island's ends 2026-01-31, so its September payment (8,580.00) is now added too. Tenbury Ridge's covers the whole period, so it's still not added. |
| Bay Crest Exteriors | Same totals | Same totals, firmer basis | Teresa Lindqvist moves to R-310 because it's the field code with the most payroll, not because of site names. Crew codes are counted in days, not hours. |
| Patuxent Electric | Unchanged | Unchanged | Nadia confirmed the flat 63,700.00 applies whatever the owner's actual wages, and the 47.00-a-day allowance cap. |
| Harbor Point Legal | Accepted | Accepted | Tomas Reyes passes the five-day test, but the firm has no field code to move him to. He stays C-110 as an open item. |

Earlier open items that interview 2 settled are now applied as company rules: holiday sign-ins are used as written and sent to the employer. Disagreements between an employer's application and its records now go on that employer's question list instead of being listed as gray areas. In [house-practice.md](skills/class-code-assistant/references/house-practice.md), the reference I keep from the two interviews, confirmed rules, gaps Nadia said she has no rule for, and my own interpretations are kept in separate lists.

## Who to call first
1. **Bay Crest Exteriors.** 319,158.10 of payroll sits in a different code from the employer's application, which put 7 of 10 people under clerical while the timesheets show 8 crew members.
2. **Larkspur Lane Bistro.** The whole catering crew (114,293.80) moves from the caterer code to the restaurant code.

Severn Homebuilders is within 2% of Larkspur, and the report says so. Of Severn's figure, 52,260.78 is added only because certificates are missing, so a call there could actually change the numbers before Friday. If Nadia would rather spend the call where it can move the figures, Severn is the better second choice.

## Remaining information gaps
- **Picking one code for mixed crew work.** Nadia confirmed days, not hours, and no splitting, but not the test that picks the single code. I use the code with the most days. Only Owen Petrakis is close (118 siding days against 97 roofing; 49,607.30 depends on it).
- **A clerical person who passes the five-day test at an employer with no field code** (Tomas Reyes, 64,212.48). Her rule has no code to move him to.
- **Things Nadia said she has no rule for.** None of these changes the six allocations:
  - an allowance paid with no travel days (Kyle Brandt, 390.00; she asked for a proposal, which is in the report);
  - a certificate in a slightly different name (Kent Island);
  - an owner who worked part of the year, or what amount applies to an owner who never does field work;
  - which source wins if the business description and payroll register disagree on the audit period.
- **Which payroll decides the field code with the most payroll** (employees only, or including subcontractor additions). This doesn't change any of the six.
- **Guide edition coverage.** Whether the July 2025 guide applies to the whole audit period is unknown; Nadia only knows the guide she has.

**On the last interview:** I don't think one is needed now. Most remaining gaps are cases Nadia already said she has no rule for, and she told us to propose, explain and flag them, which the report does. Only the mixed-crew test and Tomas Reyes could move dollars. I'd save the interview for Nadia's review of this first pass, or use it only if she disputes the "most days" choice.

## Not verified
- The interpretations above that Nadia hasn't confirmed.
- Whether the guide edition covers the full audit period.
- The "Employer's code" column in the report: the application names no one, so I paired people to its totals. It is used only to explain differences, never to classify.

## Verification and session evidence
- **What I ran:** the tests, a full run that fetches fresh from Drive, a single-employer run that produced the same CSV, the error paths, and hand recalculations for all changed totals.
- **What the validator checks:** the CSV format and `rationale_ref`, that totals and reconciliation match, that every cited record and rule exists, that every adjustment and open item is on the question list, and that no employer data is hard-coded.
- **Negative test:** I ran the validator on a deliberately broken copy, and it caught a changed cent, a fake rule label and a non-existent record file.
- **Session evidence:** each commit, including the final `b48e923`, carries an Entire checkpoint. The checkpoints are only local until you push.

# Classification guide excerpt

Linden Shore Mutual, workers' compensation, Maryland. Edition of July 2025. Internal use by underwriting and premium
audit.

This excerpt holds the general paragraphs and the class codes our current new-business employers fall under. Audit
files cite a paragraph by its identifier (CG-01, CG-02 and so on). A class code is cited by the paragraph that
describes it.

## General

**CG-01. Premium basis.** Premium is charged per USD 100 of payroll in each class code at the rate underwriting sets
for that code. Payroll is reported for the policy period being audited.

**CG-02. Assigning codes.** An employer is assigned the class code that describes its principal business. An employee
whose work is described by another code in this guide is reported under that code. An employer may carry several codes.

**CG-03. Payroll.** Payroll is the gross remuneration paid to employees for the period: wages, salaries, commissions
and bonuses. Expense reimbursements that the employer can document, such as travel and lodging costs, are not payroll.

**CG-05. Owners and executive officers.** An owner or executive officer who has filed an election of exclusion is not
counted. An owner who is included is counted under the code for the work the owner does.

**CG-06. Subcontractors.** Payments to a subcontractor who does not carry workers' compensation insurance for its own
workers may be treated as payroll of the employer, under the code for the work the subcontractor performed.

**CG-07. Division of payroll.** When an employee performs work in more than one classification and the employer keeps
records of the time spent in each, the employee's payroll may be divided between the codes.

## Class codes

**CG-04. C-110 Clerical office employees.** Employees whose duties are confined to an office: correspondence,
bookkeeping, dispatching by telephone or radio, drafting and estimating at a desk, and professional staff who work in
the office.

**CG-11. R-310 Roofing.** Installation, repair and removal of roofs and roof coverings on any building, including
work on scaffolds and ladders at the roof line.

**CG-12. R-320 Siding and gutters.** Installation and repair of exterior siding, gutters, downspouts and exterior trim
below the roof line. Roofing work is described by CG-11.

**CG-13. L-620 Landscaping and lawn care.** Lawn mowing, planting, mulching and the care of grounds.

**CG-15. H-420 Residential homebuilding.** Construction and remodeling of dwellings: framing, drywall, interior
finish, carpentry and general labor at the building site. Roofing work is described by CG-11 and electrical wiring
by CG-21.

**CG-21. E-510 Electrical wiring.** Installation and repair of electrical wiring and fixtures inside buildings,
including service connections.

**CG-22. M-830 Metal fabrication shop.** Cutting, bending and welding of sheet and structural metal in a shop.

**CG-31. T-610 Courier and delivery drivers.** Drivers of vans and light trucks delivering parcels and documents,
and helpers who ride on the delivery vehicles.

**CG-35. G-950 Parking garage attendants.** Parking and retrieving customer vehicles.

**CG-41. F-710 Restaurants.** Preparation and service of meals: kitchen staff, servers, hosts and dishwashers.

**CG-42. F-720 Off-site caterers.** Preparation of food and its service at events away from the employer's premises,
including the catering crew of an employer that also runs a restaurant.

**CG-51. N-910 Home health care.** Personal care and nursing services in clients' homes.

113	    pass differs from the employer; it never decides a classification (HP-1: not by application estimates).
114	    """
115	    codes = list(split)
116	    if len(codes) ** len(register) > 3_000_000:
117	        return None, "too many employees to pair the employer's split with people; it is compared by code only"
118	    hits = []
119	    for combo in itertools.product(codes, repeat=len(register)):
120	        counts, sums = Counter(combo), defaultdict(Decimal)
121	        if any(counts[c] != split[c]["employees"] for c in codes):
122	            continue
123	        for code, e in zip(combo, register):
124	            sums[code] += e["wages"]
125	        if all(sums[c] == split[c]["payroll"] for c in codes):
126	            hits.append(dict(zip((e["id"] for e in register), combo)))
127	            if len(hits) > 1:
128	                return None, "more than one pairing of people fits the employer's split; it is compared by code only"
129	    if not hits:
130	        return None, "no pairing of register wages reproduces the employer's split exactly; it is compared by code only"
131	    return hits[0], ("the application names no people; exactly one pairing of register wages reproduces its head count "
132	                     "and payroll for every code, so 'Employer's code' shows that pairing. It explains differences "
133	                     "only and decided no classification (HP-1)")
134	
135	
136	def allocate(guide, hp, rec, ws):
137	    res = Result(rec, ws)

139	    threshold = int(hp["clerical_job_site_day_threshold"])

141	    owner_flat = money(hp["owner_field_work_flat_payroll"])
142	    start, end = rec["period"]
143	    in_period = lambda d: start <= d <= end  # noqa: E731
144	    reg_file = rec["register_file"]
145	
146	    def code_ok(code, where):
147	        if not code:
148	            raise WorksheetError(f"{where} is not filled in; decide it from the records (see SKILL.md, step 3)")
149	        try:
150	            guide.ref_for(code)
151	        except ValueError as exc:

153	        return code
154	
155	    def applied(rule):
156	        if rule not in res.applied:

158	
159	    ws_people = ws.get("employees", {})

161	    extra = [i for i in ws_people if i not in {e["id"] for e in rec["register"]}]

166	    def out_of_period(rows, key, file):

168	        if n:
169	            res.notes.append(f"{n} row(s) in {file} fall outside the audit period and were not used.")

172	    timesheets = defaultdict(list)
173	    for r in rec["timesheets"]:
174	        if in_period(day(r["date"])):
175	            timesheets[r["employee_id"]].append(r)

183	    if others:

202	    split_people, pending, owners = [], [], []

230	                    f"House practice puts an owner who never works in the field under {clerical} but does not state the "

233	                    f"{e['name']} ({reg_file}): please confirm that {e['name']} did no field work in the audit period "

252	            final = duty if duty in leaders else leaders[0]
253	            mix = ", ".join(f"{t} {len(d)} days" for t, d in sorted(by_type.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])))

256	            p.records.append(rec["timesheets_file"])

266	                    f"{e['name']} ({rec['timesheets_file']}): {p.evidence} Please confirm which work {e['name']} "
267	                    f"mainly did during the audit period."))

269	            days = site_days[e["id"]]
270	            p.records.append(rec["signins_file"])
271	            dates = ", ".join(d.isoformat() for d in sorted(days))
272	            p.evidence = (f"{rec['signins_file']} records {e['name']} at a job site on {len(days)} day(s): " + "; ".join(
273	                f"{d.isoformat()} {', '.join(sorted(days[d]))}" for d in sorted(days)) + ".")
274	            for d in sorted(days):

277	                                             f"{rec['signins_file']} records {e['name']} at {', '.join(sorted(days[d]))} "
278	                                             f"on {d.isoformat()} ({FIXED_HOLIDAYS[(d.month, d.day)]})"))
279	                    applied("HP-15")

297	                    f"{e['name']} ({rec['route_log_file']}): please send {e['name']}'s weekly gross pay for the audit "

299	            else:
300	                p.records.append(rec["weekly_payroll_file"])
301	                per_week = [(s, t, g, sum(1 for d in rides if s <= d <= t)) for s, t, g in weeks]
302	                hist = Counter(n for *_, n in per_week)
303	                moved_weeks = [w_ for w_ in per_week if w_[3] >= min_ride]
304	                moved = sum((g for _, _, g, _ in moved_weeks), ZERO)
305	                weekly_total = sum((g for _, _, g in weeks), ZERO)

323	                    ]

335	
336	        _travel(res, hp, e, p, reg_file)

338	        res.people.append(p)

"""Read-only independent recomputation of the six first-pass allocations from the raw employer records."""
import csv, itertools, sys
from collections import defaultdict, Counter
from datetime import date, timedelta
from decimal import Decimal as D
from pathlib import Path

E = Path(sys.argv[1])
S, T = date(2025, 7, 7), date(2026, 7, 5)
d = lambda s: date.fromisoformat(s)
rows = lambda p: list(csv.DictReader(open(p, newline="")))
HOL = {date(2025, 7, 4), date(2025, 9, 1), date(2025, 11, 27), date(2025, 12, 25), date(2026, 1, 1),
       date(2026, 1, 19), date(2026, 2, 16), date(2026, 5, 25), date(2026, 6, 19), date(2025, 11, 11), date(2025, 10, 13)}

print("== pairing uniqueness (independent)")
import re
for emp in sorted(p.name for p in E.iterdir()):
    reg = rows(E / emp / "payroll-register.csv")
    app = (E / emp / "application.md").read_text()
    split = {m[0]: (int(m[1]), D(m[2])) for m in re.findall(r"\| ([A-Z]-\d{3}) \| (\d+) \| ([\d.]+) \|", app)}
    codes = list(split)
    hits = 0
    for combo in itertools.product(codes, repeat=len(reg)):
        c = Counter(combo)
        if any(c[k] != split[k][0] for k in codes):
            continue
        sums = defaultdict(D)
        for k, r in zip(combo, reg):
            sums[k] += D(r["wages_paid"])
        if all(sums[k] == split[k][1] for k in codes):
            hits += 1
    tot = sum(D(r["wages_paid"]) for r in reg)
    print(f"  {emp}: pairings={hits} register_total={tot} app_total={sum(v[1] for v in split.values())}")

print("== Annapolis")
a = E / "annapolis-courier"
rl = rows(a / "route-log.csv")
print("  route dates span", min(r["date"] for r in rl), max(r["date"] for r in rl), "rows", len(rl))
print("  driver ids", Counter(r["driver_id"] for r in rl))
print("  ride ids", Counter(r["ride_along_id"] for r in rl if r["ride_along_id"]))
print("  weekday of route days", Counter(d(r["date"]).strftime("%a") for r in rl))
route_days = {r["date"] for r in rl}
for h in sorted(HOL):
    if S <= h <= T:
        print(f"  holiday {h}: route rows={sum(1 for r in rl if r['date']==h.isoformat())}, rides={[r['ride_along_id'] for r in rl if r['date']==h.isoformat() and r['ride_along_id']]}")
wp = rows(a / "weekly-payroll.csv")
for emp_id in ("AC-E04", "AC-E05"):
    rides = sorted({d(r["date"]) for r in rl if r["ride_along_id"] == emp_id})
    wk = [(d(r["week_start"]), d(r["week_end"]), D(r["gross_pay"])) for r in wp if r["employee_id"] == emp_id]
    moved = [(s, g, sum(1 for x in rides if s <= x <= t)) for s, t, g in wk]
    m = sum(g for s, g, n in moved if n >= 2)
    hol_weeks = [(s, n, [x.isoformat() for x in rides if s <= x <= s + timedelta(6) and x in HOL]) for s, g, n in moved if n >= 2 and any(x in HOL for x in rides if s <= x <= s + timedelta(6))]
    print(f"  {emp_id}: rides={len(rides)} weeks={len(wk)} weekly_total={sum(g for *_, g in wk)} moved={m} distinct_pay={set(g for *_, g in wk)}")
    print(f"    moved weeks resting on a holiday ride: {hol_weeks}")
    multi = Counter(r["date"] for r in rl if r["ride_along_id"] == emp_id)
    print(f"    days riding >1 route: {[k for k, v in multi.items() if v > 1]}")

print("== Bay Crest")
b = E / "bay-crest-exteriors"
ts = rows(b / "crew-timesheets.csv")
print("  span", min(r["date"] for r in ts), max(r["date"] for r in ts), "hours", Counter(r["hours"] for r in ts), "types", Counter(r["work_type"] for r in ts))
code = {"roofing": "R-310", "siding": "R-320", "gutters": "R-320"}
reg = {r["employee_id"]: r for r in rows(b / "payroll-register.csv")}
whole, div = defaultdict(D), defaultdict(D)
for emp_id in sorted({r["employee_id"] for r in ts}):
    days = defaultdict(set)
    perday = defaultdict(set)
    for r in ts:
        if r["employee_id"] == emp_id:
            days[code[r["work_type"]]].add(r["date"]); perday[r["date"]].add(r["work_type"])
    w = D(reg[emp_id]["wages_paid"])
    n = sum(len(v) for v in days.values())
    top = max(days, key=lambda k: len(days[k]))
    whole[top] += w
    r310 = (w * len(days.get("R-310", ())) / n).quantize(D("0.01"))
    div["R-310"] += r310; div["R-320"] += w - r310
    print(f"  {emp_id} {reg[emp_id]['name']}: {dict((k, len(v)) for k, v in days.items())} total_days={n} mixed_days={sum(1 for v in perday.values() if len(v)>1)} holidays={[x for x in perday if d(x) in HOL]} wages={w} whole->{top} div R-310={r310} R-320={w-r310}")
print("  whole (R2):", dict(whole), " day-proportional (CG-07 alternative):", dict(div))
si = rows(b / "site-signin-log.csv")
for r in si: print("   signin", r)

print("== Harbor")
for r in rows(E / "harbor-point-legal/site-signin-log.csv"): print("   ", r, "HOL" if d(r["date"]) in HOL else "", d(r["date"]).strftime("%a"))

print("== Larkspur")
g = rows(E / "larkspur-lane-bistro/gross-receipts.csv")
off = sum(D(r["offsite_catering_receipts"]) for r in g); din = sum(D(r["dine_in_receipts"]) for r in g)
print("  months", [r["month"] for r in g][0], "...", [r["month"] for r in g][-1], len(g), "off", off, "total", off + din, "share", (off / (off + din) * 100).quantize(D("0.01")))
